Subject: RE: Production errors spiking in US-West (502/503) - affecting checkouts

Triage notes (initial):
- We've observed a surge of 502/503 responses originating at the US-WEST edge proxy tier between 07:40-08:15 PDT. Error rate peaked ~18% for a short window.
- The upstream origin (backend serving tier) is healthy based on telemetry; CPU/GPU utilization does not show saturation.
- Root cause (candidate): intermittent 502/503s appear correlated with an intermittent HTTP/1.1 keepalive exhaustion at the regional proxy due to a sudden burst of connections plus slow TLS handshakes from a subset of clients. This caused the edge LB to drop requests which surfaced as 502/503. The client-side aggressive retry loops then overloaded the token bucket which produced 429s on our API proxy.

Immediate mitigations applied at 08:00 PDT:
1) Increase proxy keepalive pool and bumped connection queue size for US-WEST.
2) Enabled local short-circuit caching for common prefix requests (non-authenticated static assets) to reduce LB churn.
3) Throttled very short backoff retries at the edge (temporary rule) for the next 30 minutes to dampen the retry storm.
4) Promoted standby nodes in US-CENTRAL to accept overflow traffic as a soft-failover path.

Status: error rate down to ~2% now, p95 latency decreased to ~160ms. We're keeping the throttles for another hour and monitoring.

Attachments (sent): usw-error-sample-logs.tar.gz (logs), diag-p90-latency-graph.png

I'll provide a follow-up with a full RCA and longer-term remediation recommendations (proxy keepalive heuristics, TLS timeout tuning, and suggestions for client retry guidelines).

- Sean
